question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution:
The correct answer is '**with**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "associated with" is a common and grammatically correct collocation in English.
 
• It is used to indicate a connection or relationship between two things — in this case, between "direct costs" and "hiring new staff."
 
• "**With**" fits best in the blank to complete the phrase "associated with hiring new staff."
 
• Other options like "**on**", "**about**", or "**behind**" do not form standard or meaningful collocations in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Reducing the hours worked and optimising shift rostering could (1)* ***help __**alleviate stress, burnout and work family (2)* *__conflict__* *for healthcare workers. All this is likely to improve staff retention. Any reduction (3)* *__in__* *staff turnaround would save on direct costs associated (4)* *__with__* *hiring new staff. The cost to replace a highly specialised healthcare professional can reach up to 200% of their annual salary. Also, (5)* **_________***shorter shifts may increase the uptake of shift times that are usually hard to fill. Measures like shorter shifts could also appeal to part time workers or those who have retired.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Behind: Indicates position or support, not appropriate in this grammatical context.
 
• About: Often indicates a topic, but does not fit idiomatically after "associated."
 
• On: Grammatically incorrect in this context with "associated."
